chapter: Le Ruban Bleu, retirement and community work
title: The youth program, kids after school and a deadline of June 1981
summary: After school from three to five kids need supervision; the House aims to give them a proving ground for performance.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: The House That Jazz Built in memory of Cliff Jackson. And so for the past five years we've had summer programs in there for kids. We expose them to jazz and listen to records, take them out on trips, take them to jazz concerts. And it's my feeling that they just don't know their enough about jazz roots and so this is what we're going to try to do from now on in with the new program. And we've selected a pretty big piece of American History. We re calling it a Hundred Years Of Jazz, from 1880 to 1980. And I think in this way they may be able to relate a little bit to history because when you consider that I'll be dealing with kids seven years old, that means that they were born in 1971. They wouldn't know anything about the swing era, boogie-woogie, bop and they are into their thing now. I'm just wondering whose going to win, me or them, because I'm going to have to listen to more of their music then they have to listen to mine. But I think the tie-in, the Board of Education, I mean, we will be working with kids that are potential delinquents or maybe truants and things like that. This might be some way of getting them interested in getting them to go back to school. That's our aim. Is to get

them back into school. There's another problem too. We don't feel that there's enough activity for these kids from the time they get out of school, that is, constructive type activity. So for four hours . . .
Especially if the mother is working.

That's right. So when the kids get out of school, from three to five, these seven to fourteen year old kids will be in our program. And of course the older kids, well it's a choice for them. They like to have fun too. They're going to be very much involved. I mean, there might be some kids out here with some talent which we hope to promote. I don't know how many kids are into music. I'm pretty sure there are some music programs in the school and these kids can play an instrument, we can get them into jazz. We can get some of our jazz bands to come up and sit in with them. This is not entirely impossible. I have a feeling that if there are kids up here that are interested that they are probably taking private lessons. But even so, this would be an ideal opportunity for them to get a chance to rehearse. They may not be allowed to practice

at home. I ran into a little boy, thirteen years old and he's into a program and he has been suspended because he didn't do so well and he's - he doesn't have access to his instrument. And so I told him to practice with his mouth piece, play the trumpet, and he said that even when he had the horn, which is the school's property-they don't exactly allow them to bring the instruments home. But on the occasions when he could his parents didn't want him practicing because, you know, a kid practicing in your house. So anyway this is going to be a thing. I'm very happy about it and I'm thinking that we're going to win.
Well I certainly hope so. I wish you every success with it.
Yes. By June of 1981 you're going to be hearing from us. We got it all planned. You're going to really be involved. I'm not going to give away my secrets now, but come back in June.
Just hang in there because I hope you'll come and sit in on us and see what we're doing, you know. It's a challenge.
